a:r.a:t: RNA Molecules Have Quite Complex Structures

p:cNvPr.descr: A complex structure of RNA using exclusively bases and base pairs. To the lower left, there is a boxed inset containing the structure of a double bonded G-U pair. On the left is the guanine, which consists of a 6-sided ring structure bonded left to a 5-sided ring structure. For the 6-sided ring, the top right C double bonds up & right to O, down and right to N, which bonds down to C, which bonds down and right to NH2 and double bonds down and left to N. N bonds left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds right to the initial O. This structure bonds left to the 5-sided ring, which contains N double bonded down and left to C, which bonds down and right to N. N bonds down and left to C (not shown) and right to C, which bonds up to C, which bonds up & left to C. The double bonded O and H on the 6-sided ring are hydrogen bonded to an H and O on the uracil, respectively. The uracil, to the right, is a 6-sided ring as well. Its lower N bonds down to C (not shown), left to C, which double bonds down to O and bonds up to N, which bonds left to H. N bonds up and right to C, which double bonded up to O. C bonds down and right to C, which double bonds down to C, which bonds down & left to N. To the right is the RNA made up of the bases and base pairs. To simplify as much as possible, the structure will be described in larger chunks before being described by the base or base pair. There are circular components and hairpin components. Beginning at the top is a hairpin component. On the left, its sequence is GCGCCCUAGCCGCC. On the left there are 2 Gs adjacent to the C and U. There is a C and A at the top of the hairpin, unbonded. On the right side, bonded to the sequence just listed, the sequence is A(labeled 160 to right)GCGGGGAUCGGUGG. There are 3 As on the right side of the hairpin structure. The bonds are all blue lines; G and U are shown bonded by a blue dot. The hairpin structure is connected downward to a large circle made of unpaired bases. The circle has multiple hairpin invaginations that will be included as turns. Left and right turns are relative to the reader. Beginning at the top left portion of the circle, where the hairpin meet it, the sequence all the way around is AA(140)AGCAGAGAACAACGUGACCAGCAG(120)CAC(right turn)CCAA(U-turn)AGGGG(right turn)GGG(left turn)GUCCGC(100)AA(U-turn)UGGACC(right turn)GCCUCAAAUGGCACGG(right turn)UGCC(220)UGACAAU(U-turn)GGUCGGCGC(right turn)GCC(right turn)CCA(200)CGCGAGAA(U-turn)UGGCGUGG(right turn)GAAA(180)GUGG(right turn)GUGGCUAGGGCGA(160)AC(U-turn)GCGCCCUAGCCGCC(left turn)A. This is a complete circle, plus a total of 5 hairpins/invaginations. There are random displaced G and A bases around the final hairpin. Below this is another section of the RNA with multiple hairpins, circles, and invaginations. Every base pair that is not part of a circle is bonded together with a blue line (i.e. anytime turns are indicated). Directional turns indicate the direction a chain of bases is heading. The number indicates a base’s place in the chain. There is a stem leading down from the large circle just described. On the left, its sequence begins: UGGG(left turn)ACGGG(U-turn)AU(80)AC(right turn)CUCG(left turn)GGCCUGAAAGGAG(left turn)G(60)GGGAGGCGGGCAGAGGGGGCU(40)(U-turn)UCUCCUGCUGCUCGUUCGCC(20)(right turn)GCUGACAG(left turn)ACCAGUCAGGAG(1)(downward terminal chain)CACCU(377). The initial C in the terminal chain initiates the other direction of bases with sequence: (right turn)UUUUGACUGG(sharp right turn)UAU(360)UUCGGCCCAAGACAGCACC(right turn)UGUCAGU(right turn)AAGUA(330)GAU(right turn)CCGGUCGUUAGC(U-turn)GAGUGAGGCAG(right turn)UUCG(300)UC(right turn)GG(right turn)AUGGGC(right turn)CCAAGUCAUG(280)CCC(U-turn)GGCAUG(up turn)GA(U-turn)AUA(left turn)CUUGGG(260)(left turn)GAUAAAC(down turn)CG(left turn)GAAC(up turn)GAGGCCC(240)AC. This final AC connects back to the circle initially described.
